title: Non-Perturbative Vibrational Excitation by Arbitrary Electric Fields from Classical Phase-Space Dynamics
authors: Sameernandan Upadhyayula, Jiří J. L. Vaníček
abstract: We present a non-perturbative framework for the quantum treatment of vibrational excitation in molecular systems driven by electric fields with arbitrary time dependence. For harmonic potentials with linear dipole coupling, the field-induced dynamics is exactly described by a displaced coherent state, whose evolution is completely determined by a complex phase-space coordinate. Closed-form expressions for this coordinate reveal a clear distinction between resonant and non-resonant regimes. The resulting vibrational populations follow a Poisson distribution determined by a dimensionless time-dependent phase-space displacement, for both resonant and non-resonant driving. Resonant driving results in an enhanced phase-space displacement, whereas finite detuning between the driving and vibrational frequencies leads to an exponential suppression of the phase-space displacement and vibrational excitation. While the approach reduces to the standard time-dependent perturbation theory in the weak-field limit, it remains valid in the strong-field regime, where perturbative treatments fail. Our results provide a transparent phase-space picture of vibrational control and enable non-perturbative state preparation in ultrafast spectroscopy.
summary: This paper introduces a non-perturbative method to model how molecular vibrations are excited by strong, time-varying electric fields. By mapping the dynamics onto a complex phase-space coordinate, the authors provide a unified description that accurately predicts vibrational populations in both resonant and non-resonant regimes. This framework is crucial for understanding and controlling molecular energy transfer in intense light fields.
main_problem: Developing a non-perturbative quantum framework to describe vibrational excitation in molecular systems driven by arbitrarily time-dependent external electric fields.
main_result: The dynamics are exactly mapped onto the evolution of a complex phase-space coordinate, yielding a Poisson distribution for vibrational populations that correctly captures both resonant enhancement and non-resonant suppression.
method: The authors utilize an exact coherent-state solution for the driven harmonic oscillator, allowing the analysis to remain valid in the strong-field regime where standard time-dependent perturbation theory fails.
model_or_system: The system models a single normal mode of a molecule with a harmonic potential and a linear dipole coupling ($\mu(q) = \mu_0 + \mu'_0 T \cdot q$) interacting with an external electric field $\vec{E}(t)$.
key_observables: Vibrational populations ($P_n(t)$), the time-dependent phase-space displacement ($S_t = |z_t|^2$), and the phase-space trajectory governed by $z_t$.
important_parameters: Resonant vs. non-resonant driving ($\omega$ vs. $\omega_0$), field strength ($E_0$), and detuning ($\Delta$).
main_assumptions: The dipole operator is approximated by an affine function of the normal coordinate ($q$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase-space trajectories for resonant (outward spiral) and non-resonant driving, and compare the results of the exact coherent-state method against Time-Dependent Perturbation Theory (TDPT) in both weak and strong-field limits.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the non-perturbative coherent-state formalism, derives the closed-form expression for the phase-space coordinate $z_t$, analyzes the distinct behaviors in resonant and non-resonant regimes, and validates the approach by showing its reduction to TDPT in the weak-field limit.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, non-perturbative phase-space picture for controlling molecular vibrations using intense light fields, which is central to ultrafast spectroscopy and quantum control.
